parole.significato: The idea that there is no separate self or soul; egolessness. One of the three marks of existence.
parole.testo: From Pali anattan, from Sanskrit अनात्मन् (anātman, “no soul”), from अन्- (an-, “non-, un-, a-”) + आत्मन् (ātman, “soul”).

parole.significato: Any other person considered similarly enlightened.
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Pali Buddha (“the Awakened One, the Enlightened One”), from buddha (“awakened, enlightened”), from Sanskrit बुद्ध (buddha, “awakened, enlightened”), past participle of बोधति (bodhati, “to wake, to awaken”). Distantly related to English bid and bede. Also cognate with Proto-Sla

parole.significato: Eight rules that are observed by lay Buddhists on observance days and festivals: to abstain from (i) taking life, (ii)…
parole.testo: Calque of Pali aṭṭha-sīla, aṭṭhaṅga-sīla or Calque of Sanskrit अष्टा-सील (aṣṭā-sīla), अष्टाण्ग-शील (aṣṭāṇga-śīla).
From Pali theravāda, from Sanskrit स्थविरवाद (sthaviravāda).

parole.significato: A regular day of fasting, devotion, or other religious observation
parole.testo: Borrowed from Pali uposatha, derived from Sanskrit उपवसथ (upavasatha, “dwelling with [the gods], a fasting day, especially before a soma sacrifice”).
